result:
Each week's heading now has a checkbox that marks all that week's runs done in one click, and the page doesn't move. All the tests pass on temporary copies of the project, and the real database and the login and signup templates are untouched. I also clicked the checkboxes with a script in real Chrome, on a temporary copy of the app:

| Action (1100px window) | Scroll position | Week's done km | Week checkbox | Runs crossed out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Start | 193 | 0 of 10 km | Unticked | 0 |
| Tick the week | 193 | 10 of 10 km | Ticked | 3 |
| Untick the week | 193 | 0 of 10 km | Unticked | 0 |
| Tick one run | 193 | 2.5 of 10 km | Unticked | 1 |

A 400px window gave the same results (scroll stayed at 177), and the other weeks didn't change.

**How it behaves**
- **Partly done week:** it shows unticked, and clicking it marks the remaining runs done.
- **Single-run checkboxes:** these work as before and update the week's checkbox. Ticking the last run ticks it, and unticking any run unticks it.
- **Week with no runs:** no checkbox, just the heading.
- **Race week:** the race counts as one of the week's runs, so ticking race week marks the race done, and it counts in your running history.
- **A page left open:** the checkbox asks for a specific state rather than flipping it, so an old page can't do the opposite of what it showed.
- **Whose runs it changes:** only the logged-in user's active plan, for that week. My test confirms other plans and other users aren't affected.

**Things you should know**
- **Unticking discards a partly done state:** if you've done two of three runs, ticking the week and then unticking it leaves all three not done, as you specified. It doesn't remember which two were done.
- **Back button:** each click adds a Back step, the same as the single-run checkboxes.

**Files changed:** `main.py`, `templates/week_frame.html` and `static/style.css`.
